abstract: A quantum algorithm is presented for the simulation of arbitrary Markovian dynamics of a qubit, described by a semigroup of single qubit quantum channels $\{T_{t}\}$ specified by a generator $\mathcal{L}$. This algorithm requires only $\mathcal{O}\big((||\mathcal{L}||_{(1\rightarrow 1)}t)^{3/2}/\epsilon^{1/2}\big)$ single qubit and CNOT gates and approximates the channel $T_{t}=e^{t\mathcal{L}}$ up to chosen accuracy $\epsilon$. Inspired by developments in Hamiltonian simulation, a decomposition and recombination technique is utilised which allows for the exploitation of recently developed methods for the approximation of arbitrary single-qubit channels. In particular, as a result of these methods the algorithm requires only a single ancilla qubit, the minimal possible dilation for a non-unitary single-qubit quantum channel.

specification.problem: Simulate an arbitrary Markovian (semigroup) qubit channel T_t = e^{tL} generated by L, approximating it to accuracy epsilon with single-qubit and CNOT gates and a single ancilla qubit, using a decomposition and recombination technique built on methods for approximating arbitrary single-qubit channels.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Abstract-level reconstruction only: the problem statement, gate-complexity scaling, and dilation claim. The explicit decomposition, recombination, and channel-approximation circuits are not given in the abstract and are not reconstructed.

symbols.meaning: single-qubit quantum channel at time t in the semigroup
symbols.domain: CPTP maps on a qubit, t>=0

equations.label: Semigroup channel
equations.description: The channel to be approximated is the exponential of the generator.
equations.abstract_quote: approximates the channel $T_{t}=e^{t\mathcal{L}}$ up to chosen accuracy $\epsilon$

equations.label: Gate complexity
equations.description: Number of single-qubit and CNOT gates required.

registers.name: system
registers.role: qubit on which the channel T_t acts

registers.name: ancilla
registers.role: single dilation qubit for the non-unitary channel, reset or discarded after each segment

specification.initial_state: System qubit in an arbitrary input state rho; ancilla in a fixed reference state (assumed |0>).

steps.description: Decompose the evolution time into segments (e.g. T_t = (T_{t/n})^n) and decompose each short-time channel into simpler pieces, in the spirit of Hamiltonian-simulation decomposition; the exact decomposition is not given in the abstract.
Approximate each piece as an arbitrary single-qubit channel using the single-ancilla dilation, implemented with single-qubit gates and CNOTs.
Recombine the approximated pieces sequentially, reusing the single ancilla, to approximate T_t to accuracy epsilon with the stated gate count.

specification.measurement: The abstract specifies no measurement. Assumed: the ancilla is traced out (discarded or reset) and the system qubit is read out in a chosen basis (e.g. Pauli X, Y, Z) over repeated runs, or full state tomography is performed, to compare the output with T_t(rho).
specification.classical_postprocessing: Assumed: estimate expectation values of Pauli observables from the measurement counts and reconstruct the output Bloch vector. Compare it with the exact e^{tL}(rho), to within accuracy epsilon, as a check. No postprocessing is given in the abstract.
assumptions: Equations are limited to those stated in the abstract.
Register sizes follow the single-ancilla claim; the ancilla initial state |0> and reuse via reset are assumed.
Step structure is a generic reading of 'decomposition and recombination' and not the paper's actual circuit.
Segmenting time as T_t=(T_{t/n})^n is an assumed illustration.
Measurement and postprocessing are assumed generic readout, not taken from the paper.
